newsitem.title: USA: Motorola signs $108 million deal in China.
newsitem.headline: Motorola signs $108 million deal in China.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Wednesday the Fujian Posts and Telecommunications Administration signed three contracts totalling $108 million for Motorola to provide cellular phone infrastructure in the Chinese province of Fujian.

As part of the deal, Fujian PTA's Global System for Mobile (GSM) Communications digital network and its Total Access Communications System (TACS) analog system will be expanded and upgraded to cover the entire Fujian province.
Shipment of the equipment is expected to begin in December of this year with commercial service planned for the first quarter of 1997.
The contracts increase the overall capacity of the analog and digital networks to 490,000 subscribers from 280,000.
The deployment of the Motorola equipment throughout the Fujian province marks the third phase of expansion for the operator's GSM network and the sixth phase of expansion for its TACS network.
In addition to the expansion of the GSM and TACS networks, Motorola Asia Pacific Cellular Infrastructure Group, the group handling the contracts, will deploy a DCS 1800 trial system in Fujian.
For the GSM system, Motorola APCIG will provide digital base stations including the the M-Cell and M-Cell micro series products.

As part of the TACS system expansion and upgrade, Motorola will install new fully self-contained MICROC-I-T-E base stations and additional EMX(R) 2500 large-capacity switches. In addition, various existing Motorola LD/TACS base stations will be upgraded.
